svg.aria-label: Sequence diagram of reads around an overwrite: Writer, Reader, Hot tier, Cold tier. A read before the replace gets the old object from hot. A read after the replace and before the acknowledgement gets the old or the new object, whole. A read after the acknowledgement always gets the new object from hot. Where the old object was only in cold, a read before the acknowledgement is served from cold and its copy-back request does nothing because the entry exists; after the acknowledgement hot holds the new object.
svg.title: A get during an overwrite: every response is one whole version; after the ack it is the new one
svg.text: A get during an overwrite: every response is one whole version; after the ack it is the new one
Writer
Reader
Hot tier
Cold tier
hot holds v1 and cold holds v1 (the steady state, no entry)
R1 open_read key: one hot call
v1, whole (a body in flight when the replace lands stays v1)
W1 overwrite: take entry, replace hot on its tag (diagram: overwrite put)
R2 open_read key, after the replace, before the ack
v2 whole (v1 was equally allowed: the put is not acknowledged yet)
W2 CAS entry to (PUT,PENDING,replace): ACK POINT
R3 open_read key, after the ack: hot is never the old version
v2, whole
the old object was only in cold (evicted), the overwrite is in flight
R4 open_read key: hot miss
R5 cold open_read key: v1, whole (the request began before the ack)
R6 ask copy-back: create-only entry, EXISTS (the overwrite holds it): nothing
Each response is one call to one tier and one object, so it is one version; a client that reads a large object in ranges sends If-Match with the
ETag of its first response and gets 412 if the object changed (section 4: the match accepts the tag of either tier that holds the version). Hot is
replaced atomically (a rename on dir:, one PUT on S3). After the ack, hot holds the new version until it is evicted, and it is evicted only after
the leader has made cold hold the same bytes, so a hot miss after the ack finds the new version in cold. A get never reads an entry on a hit.
